title: Cutover simulation lab notes & Terraform operator checklist
content:
Purpose:
This doc records lab-run results and a pragmatic checklist for cutovers that use the Terraform Operator (tf-operator) mode in private deployments (VPC / on‑prem). The goal is to provide: repeatable simulation steps, concrete canary thresholds and switchback logic, operator-specific rollback triggers, and a short test matrix for API compatibility verification.

Scope and assumptions:
- Applies to private deployments controlled by our control plane (private control plane + runtime agents) using tf-operator to apply cluster resources and runtime configuration.
- Target upgrade types in lab: runtime binary upgrades, control plane component (api-gateway, auth proxy) and API surface changes requiring client shims.
- Lab environment mirrors customer private topology: 3 AZ-equivalent nodes, one controlplane proxy, one shared KV, single-model serving runtime pool.
- We assume feature-flagging and model-pin mechanisms are available to route traffic to old/new runtime variants.

High-level approach:
1. Create isolated lab copy of customer manifests (terraform state + provider configs) and a sandbox Concourse job that uses tf-operator in dry-run mode.
2. Run an automated canary pipeline that: deploys new runtime variant to a subset, runs synthetic load and regression tests, monitors SLOs and error budgets, then promotes or switches back automatically based on thresholds.
3. Record metrics and failure modes; capture rollback sequences and operator-level reconcile logs for postmortem template.

Lab setup checklist (quick):
- [ ] Clone customer's TF state export into lab bucket (state-export-<customer>-<date>.tfstate).
- [ ] Replace production secrets with lab KMS keys and test certs (never use prod keys).
- [ ] Deploy tf-operator in two modes: dry-run (plan-only) and live (apply). Verify RBAC and CRD health.
- [ ] Start monitoring stack (Prometheus-in-Lab + Grafana) with the same metric names and tag structure as prod (latency.p95, token_cost_per_request, kv_hit_rate).
- [ ] Create synthetic clients (k6 + curl harness) that reproduce customer token mix and sequence lengths.

Terraform operator notes (practical tips):
- Operator mode toggle: use upstream CRD flux for 'spec.applyMode' = ["PlanOnly","ForceApply"]. During lab rehearsals always start with PlanOnly and validate diff artifacts.
- Drift detection: enable tf-operator's periodic-plan (every 5m) and capture plan artifacts. Set a gating rule: any plan that touches resource types in [statefulset, pvc, service] must create a manual approval ticket.
- Immutable fields: runtime pods have several immutable fields (nodeSelector, taints) — prefer rolling update via service/label switch rather than Recreate for these.
- Locking: ensure state lock (Dynamo/Consul) is emulated; simulate a failed lock to observe operator retry/backoff logic.

Simulation scenarios (ordered small->large):
- Smoke plan-only: operator makes no changes; validate plans and stop. Expected: zero runtime traffic impact.
- Non-disruptive config change: update configmap for batch size or kv cache TTL. Expected: rolling reloads, no inference errors.
- Binary-only runtime upgrade (same model API): deploy new runtime image tagged canary-2025-01. Expected: model behavior unchanged; measure latency and memory.
- API surface change (minor): add optional query param or response field. Expected: old clients ignore new fields; run backward-compat tests.
- API surface change (breaking): remove endpoint or rename field. Use shim sidecar in controlplane to maintain compatibility, plan switch with gradual client rollout.

Canary plan and thresholds (auto decision rules):
- Canary population: 3 replicas (10% of traffic) initially, scale to 10% and 30% in two steps.
- Observation window: 5m at each step (short test) then 30m for extended validation.
- Hard reject conditions (immediate rollback):
  - error_rate_increase > 0.5% absolute AND error_rate_relative > 200%
  - p95 latency increase > 200ms AND > 30% relative
  - model response mismatch (semantic drift) above 2% on evaluation prompts
  - memory OOMs or >95% memory utilization on any instance
- Soft reject (hold and notify):
  - token_cost_per_request deviation > 12%
  - throughput drop > 10% without latency change
- Promotion criteria: sustained SLO compliance for 30m, no errors beyond baseline, and quality regression < 0.25% on eval set.

Automated rollback triggers (operator-level):
- Tie tf-operator hooks to the canary pipeline: if monitoring webhook sends a FAIL state, operator should annotate the CR with revert=true and apply a rollback plan that restores the previous replica set and runtime_image tag.
- Maintain previous successful terraform plan as 'golden-plan' artifact. Rolling back is: apply golden-plan -> wait for resource readiness -> run smoke tests -> mark success.
- Implement a two-minute cool-off: if manual intervention occurs, latch auto-rollback for at least 2m to avoid flip-flopping.

API compatibility checks (test matrix):
- Contract tests (automated): success responses, required fields, authentication headers, rate-limit headers.
- Fuzz tests: run random payloads to both old and new runtime to detect divergent failures.
- Regression eval set: 1k prompts covering prompt templates, long-context, function-calling mocks; compare output quality and parseability.
- Client integration smoke: run 3 client SDK versions (latest, previous, previous-2) and verify no request timeouts or signature failures.

Observability + quick runbook (what to watch):
- Metrics to stream to Ops channel: p50/p95 latency, request_errors, kv_hit_rate, model_evals_failed, pod_restart_count, image_pull_errors.
- Logs: operator reconcile events, terraform plan diffs, kubernetes events for pods/pvc.
- Alerts (pager):
  - P1: runtime OOMs, pod crashloop > 3x in 10m, any p95 spike > 2x baseline.
  - P2: plan failures that touch stateful resources, apply stuck > 10m.

Known risks and mitigations:
- Risk: TF operator applying a destructive plan for PVC or DB migration. Mitigation: manual approval gate + additive-only plan enforcement for critical resources.
- Risk: Canary too small to catch intermittent regressions. Mitigation: run longer observation windows and parallel chaos testing (network latency injection).
- Risk: Drift between lab and prod TF state. Mitigation: snapshot and hash check; fail if delta > 1% of resources.

Post-simulation artifacts (what to save):
- golden-plan-<timestamp>.tfplan and diff summary (attach to ticket).
- Prometheus time-series export for the full run window.
- Operator reconcile logs (one file) and all plan artifacts.
- Short postmortem template prefilled with timeline, decision points, and recommended guardrails.

Action items (next steps):
- [ ] Create a reusable lab CI job that replays the last 6 months of client traffic for a target customer. (Assignee: Jon)
- [ ] Add plan-only policy to tf-operator CRDs for critical resources. (Assignee: Miguel)
- [ ] Build a small shim sidecar for API backward compatibility for field-level renames. (Assignee: Ella)
- [ ] Draft an SRE runbook for automatic rollback thresholds. (Assignee: Samir)

Notes to reviewers:
- This is intentionally pragmatic; we trade some automation complexity for safer, repeatable rehearsals. Please add any missing failure modes you want covered in the simulation matrix.
- If we get buy-in for golden-plan artifacts and a plan approval workflow, I can convert these steps into a Concourse pipeline and a tf-operator controller extension.

End of lab notes.
